harmonicFunction: C (I) - Tonic chord establishing warmth and home
C/B (I/7) - Inversion passing chord providing the descending bass step on fret 2 string 5
Am (vi) - Relative minor chord introducing introspective wistfulness
F (IV) - Subdominant chord introducing tenderness and hope
G (V) - Dominant chord propelling the cadence smoothly back to C

techniques.name: Stepwise Descending Bass Walkdown
techniques.description: Moving smoothly from C (root on 5th string 3rd fret) to C/B (5th string 2nd fret) to Am (open 5th string), letting treble strings ring continuously

sequence: Pluck the 5th string 3rd fret for C on beat 1
Walk down to the 5th string 2nd fret for C/B on beat 3
Resolve to the open 5th string for Am on the next measure
Maintain smooth, gentle acoustic arpeggiation throughout
tips: Use your 2nd finger for the B note in C/B while keeping your 1st finger on the 2nd string 1st fret (C note)
Do not rush the slow 72 BPM tempo — space is the soul of this ballad
Fmaj7 (X-X-3-2-1-0) works beautifully if full barre F feels too heavy

beginner.title: Master the Walkdown Shapes
steps: Practice changing between C and C/B (moving 2nd finger to 5th string 2nd fret)
Connect smoothly from C/B to open Am
Play the 4-chord verse cycle at 60 BPM
Bring up to album tempo of 72 BPM

intermediate.title: Dynamic Chorus & Bridge Nuance
steps: Practice full barre F chord transitions from G and C
Master the ii-V-I bridge progression (Dm - G - C)
Work on dynamic builds from tender verse to powerful chorus

advanced.title: Complete Acoustic Interpretation
steps: Integrate fingerpicked arpeggio flourishes across upper strings
Perform the full emotional vocal and guitar accompaniment
Deliver the quintessential Australian campfire ballad

commonMistakes: Rushing the 72 BPM tempo — ballad timing requires patient spacing
Muting the open G string when fretting the C/B chord
Fretting the F chord sloppily during the chorus
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Isolated C → C/B → Am walkdown drill
5 minutes: Verse arpeggio picking at 72 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus G → F → C transitions
metronomeWork: Practice at 60 BPM with metronome clicks on all four beats
Advance to 72 BPM once chord transitions are fluid
Practice with metronome on beats 2 and 4 for natural sway
